findings.title: Equivalent C08 writes make witnessed historical choice unavailable before its exact resultRef can disambiguate ancestry
findings.mechanism: W2 selects every C08 with matching requestDigest/resultDigest, chooses the greatest case version and rejects latest.length != 1 before using ChoiceRecord.comparison.alternativeResultRef. The result writer allows equivalent results with different idempotency keys and resultRefs at the same DecisionCase.version. A legitimate chosen original becomes unavailable after alternative v1 to v2, despite an exact choice ledger witness. A later eligible equivalent record can likewise be preferred over the witnessed original.
findings.impact: Historical read fails closed for a valid persisted choice; availability/ancestry selection defect, not an access grant.
static_reproduction: Persist C08 A for alternative v1.
Persist the same result/request at the same case version with a new idempotency key, obtaining C08 B.
Record the human choice with comparison.alternativeResultRef pointing to A.
W2 historical reader rejects equivalent A+B before using the choice witness.
findings.followup_assessment: The reviewed local correction collects witnessed choices even when a transaction snapshot exists, filters matching C08 records by exact witnessed alternativeResultRef before ambiguity selection, and rejects missing/ambiguous witnessed provenance. With no witnessed choice it preserves the conservative latest-record ambiguity rule. No concrete regression identified in this correction.
findings.test_delta: The existing real ChoiceRecord history test now writes an equivalent C08 through results.write with a distinct idempotency key, asserts distinct ref and equal case/result digest, records the choice using the original ref, revises v1 to v2 and requires recovery of that original ref. Revoked C08 and tampered-ledger negatives remain.

assertions_reviewed.observation: The fixture persists the two scenario results with the real C08 store, invokes createPlannerPort.compareScenarios over those persisted refs and persists the canonical comparison. Expected knownDifference=20 is conditioned; completeDifference and the unavailable-rule criterion value remain null/unknown.

The initial case has choices=[] and ledger=[]. The fixture calls createDecisionMutations.recordChoice, first checks refusal without confirmation, then reads the resulting choice from the case. It checks exact comparison, scenario operations, principal/reason, one choice-recorded event and its outputDigest, and an idempotent retry. The previous fake ChoiceRecord cast is removed.

The candidate ref pins the same post-choice case/version and alternative. Portfolio evaluation reads the persisted C08 scenario and comparison. preparePortfolioChoice refuses before the preparation grant, then delegates to real WP11 preparation. It asserts two planned effects with expectedVersion=4 and unchanged controlled domain amounts.

The application path uses createPreparedExecution and createSfPreparedApply with proposalReviewDigest and receiptReviewBinding. It refuses before apply confirmation and asserts no mutation. After confirmation it requires first execution ok, exactly one authoritative receipt, immediate case reconciliation, applied/planned states, unchanged ChoiceRecord digest and an identical retry result. This matches the local WP11 fresh-CAS reconciliation logic; no case-reconciliation-pending success surrogate remains.

The controlled Procurement mutation is initially unavailable; the case remains partially-applied with one receipt and Planner already applied. On resume the test requires both effects applied, amounts [40,60], exactly one execution per domain, two durable receipts, review-proof transaction digests matching the prepared changes, and unchanged choice/scenario/comparison digests. It retries both completed effects without duplicating execution.

assessment.area: Admitted input and boolean verification result
assessment.observation: incoming is cloned before the first await and the full admitted digest is captured. All verification reads use the private stored snapshot. Before returning true, after the final host revalidation, the original incoming object must still have the admitted digest. This prevents a true boolean result from approving a caller object that changed during verification.

caseFor, readHistoricalBinding, cases.read and evidence.context results are cloned immediately after their awaited returns. The two inspection records therefore retain independent observations even if providers reuse mutable objects. The existing historical-candidate callback was already cloned.

readHistoricalBinding receives a clone of current.value, and evidence.context receives a clone of stored.sourceRefs. Provider mutation of those arguments cannot rewrite the private inspected case/evidence snapshot.

The same-version admission/future-version rejection, binding/selection/request/result/candidate digest comparisons, evidence reference equality/accessRevision, historical/fresh policy and repeated host revalidation remain in place.

The test mutates a private incoming clone during caseFor, expects false and asserts the caller mutation is not undone. With the new input snapshot, this specifically requires the final incoming digest comparison; snapshot alone would approve the old admitted content while the caller object had changed.

The test returns a shared owner object and mutates its version only during the first binding read. The first observation remains at its original version and differs from the second. This discriminates the copy boundary: without the caseFor clone, the first record could absorb that one-time mutation and both passes could agree.

limitations: Static review only; no local product execution, CI dispatch, typecheck or remote verification by this reviewer.
